## Full-Time Flat-Rate Tuition

* * *

See the flat-rate tuition rates for New Jersey residents and out-of-state students.

Residency  | Tuition Rate
--- | ---
New Jersey residents  | $3,595
Out-of-state residents  | $4,652

  * Students registering for 9 or more credits per term will receive the discounted Full-Time Flat-Rate Tuition.
  * Students do not have to preselect this plan, but will be automatically enrolled once the 9-credit per term threshold has been reached.
  * Students registering for fewer than 9 credits per term will continue to be enrolled under Per Credit Tuition. Learn more about undergraduate tuition.

## Per Credit Tuition

* * *

Explore the per credit tuition rates for different student types below.

Residency  | Per Credit Registered
--- | ---
New Jersey Residents*  | $449
Out-of-state Residents  | $584
Visiting (In-State)  | $612
Visiting (Out-of-State)  | $612

* Includes Pennsylvania residents

  * Students to register and pay for courses on a per credit basis
  * Per Credit Tuition does not cover textbooks or course materials

## Credit-Hour Residency Requirement

* * *

Students who use Per Credit Tuition (excluding those who enroll under a military plan) with the intention of earning an associate or bachelor’s degree from Thomas Edison State University must complete 15 credits via Thomas Edison State University online (OL), Guided Study (GS) or e-Pack (EP) courses. This requirement may be waived by paying the Edison Accelerate fee.

## Notes:

* * *

  * If your degree program requires a course not offered by Thomas Edison State University, then you may need to take that course at another institution. Those courses are not covered by either tuition plan, and you would be responsible for any and all costs incurred at that institution.
  * Per Credit Tuition does not apply to nursing students or graduate students.
  * The Full-Time Flat-Rate Tuition plan does not apply to nonmatriculated, nursing, military or graduate-program students.
  * The Full-Time Flat-Rate Tuition Plan does not include TECEP and PLA registrations. Eligible students that register for 9 or more credits of Online (OL), Guided Study (GS) and/or E-packs, in addition to a TECEP and/or PLA will be charged the respective rate for the TECEP and/or PLA registered course separately.
  * See the University’s Tuition and Fee Descriptions, Refund Policy and Past Due Delinquent Account Policy

NOTE: All tuition and fees listed here were approved on June 12, 2026, by the Board of Trustees of TESU and are effective August 2026 term. Tuition and fees are subject to change.

# Accelerated Courses

## Overview of Academic Courses and Schedules

  * catalog
  * General Education Courses
  * Online Courses
  * e-Pack Courses
  * Nursing Courses
  * pla-courses
  * Self-Directed Courses
  * Zero Textbook Cost (ZTC) Courses
  * Guided Study Courses
  * Accelerated Courses
  * Taking Courses

Starting in July 2026, we are launching a new way for you to power through your degree.

By adapting our Guided Study courses into a fast-paced, 4-week format, you can now earn credits faster and more affordably using Accelerated Courses.

These 4-week independent study courses enable students to work in an accelerated fashion on their own to complete course assignments and take examinations. Like our e-Pack® courses, students taking Accelerated Courses have no interaction with classmates.

## Basics of the 4-Week Format

* * *

  * What are accelerated courses?

These are 4-week versions of our existing Guided Study courses. They are designed for undergraduate students who already have some familiarity with the subject matter and want to progress quickly.

  * Do Accelerated Courses require fewer assignments and exams than online or Guided Study courses?

Accelerated courses require the same amount of work in each course as online and Guided Study courses. Per TESU’s Credit Hour Policy, please expect to spend 48 hours per week for each three (3) credit accelerated course. Students who have previous knowledge or experience in the subject of the course may be more comfortable in the Accelerated Courses.

  * How often are they offered?

We offer three consecutive four (4)-week sessions within every 12-week term.

  * Who can take them?

Any undergraduate student can elect to take these courses.

  * How many credits can I earn?

By taking one course in every four (4)-week session, you can earn up to 36 credits (12 courses) per year. You can take more though, up to 16 credits in any 12-week period, usually under one term.

## Academic Flexibility and Pacing

* * *

  * Are there set due dates for assignments?

No. Accelerated courses do not have individual assignment due dates or late-penalty policies. Your grade is based on whatever coursework and exams you submit by the end of the four (4)-week session. However, to show "academic engagement" and remain eligible for financial aid, you must complete at least Module 1 by the end of the second week of the session.

  * What if I need more time?

We offer a no-cost eight (8)-week course extension upon request. Unlike other formats, you do not need a mentor's certification or a requirement to have 50% of the work completed to ask for this extension.

  * Can I mix course lengths?

Yes! You can mix four (4)-week, 12-week, and (for Bachelor’s to Master’s or Nursing students) 8-week graduate courses all in one term.

  * When can I expect my final course grade to be released?

Grades are released within 9 days after the end of each session.

## Tuition and Financial Aid

* * *

  * How does this save me money?

You can take advantage of the Full-time Flat Rate Tuition without needing to take 9 credits all at once. Instead, you can spread those 9+ credits across the three consecutive four (4)-week sessions.

  * Can I use Financial Aid?

Yes, federal and state Financial Aid can be used for these courses. To remain eligible and show "academic engagement," you must complete at least Module 1 by the end of the second week of the session.

If you are using Financial Aid, you must select accelerated courses in sessions within the same overarching term. For example, if you are in an Accelerated course in July 2026 Session 1 and want to take another course starting in early August, you must select July 2026 Session 2. If you select a course in a session in any term other than July 2026, it will not be covered by your FA. Each term offers three sessions in which to take courses and for FA, all your courses must be in the same overarching term.

Some accelerated sessions have sessions in different terms that start on the same day, so be sure to register only for the term you were awarded your Financial Aid.

  * Can I use military Tuition Assistance?

If you are using military tuition assistance for Accelerated courses, you must provide the exact four-week session dates on your TA request form, not the full 12-week term dates.

For example, if you are in an Accelerated course in July 2026 Session 1, you must use June 29 to July 26, 2026 as the course dates when requesting TA. If you want to take a course in July 2026 Session 2, you must use July 27 to August 23, 2026 as the course dates on your TA request form. Your TA will be rejected if sent to the University and the dates of the courses do not match the specific course dates for the courses you’ve registered for.

  * When is tuition due?

Payment of tuition for Session 1 is required at the point of registration, unless approved TESU FA is in place. Students may delay payment for Session 2 and Session 3 courses until 3pm on the Friday before the Session starts. Unpaid tuition at that point will result in deregistration.

  * Refund Policy

    * 100% refund if dropped before Session Day 1.
    * 50% refund if dropped before Session Day 7.


## Registration and Degrees

* * *

  * Which degrees can be completed entirely through these courses?

Several popular programs are designed to be completed using only accelerated courses:

    * BA in Liberal Studies (General, Computer Science, or Humanities concentrations)
    * BS in General Management
    * AA in General Studies
    * AS in Business Management or Computer Science
    * AAS in Construction and Facility Support

  * How can I find the Accelerated Course offerings each term?

In Self-Service, use the filter to search for a specific term, then under Course Type, filter for Accelerated Session 1, Accelerated Session 2 and Accelerated 3. You will find the Accelerated sections listed with a section code of AC, as opposed to OL for online, NU for Nursing or GS for Guided Study.

  * Can I still add a course if the term has already started?

Yes. You can add or drop courses for future four (4)-week sessions while the overall term is still ongoing, right up until the day the specific session starts. There is no late registration fee for these courses.

If you are using Financial Aid, you must select sessions within the same overarching term. For example, if you are in an accelerated course in July 2026 Session 1 and want to take another course starting in early August, you must select July 2026 Session 2. If you select a course in a session in any term other than July 2026, it will not be covered by your FA. Each term offers three sessions in which to take courses and for FA, all your courses must be in the same overarching term.

  * Do the Accelerated Courses count toward my TESU residency requirement?

Yes, the Accelerated Courses do count toward your residency requirement of 15 credits for traditional or nursing students and 12/24 for active military students.

  * Can I use the Accelerated courses in my Bachelor’s to Master’s program?

Absolutely. Admitted bachelor’s students can earn up to 12 graduate credits to apply toward both their Bachelor’s and a future Master’s degree. For example, BS in General Management students can take graduate courses toward an MBA, M.S. in Management, or M.S. in Healthcare Management. Speak to your advisor to plan this out.

  * When will I become enrolled if I am taking an Accelerated course?

You will become an enrolled student on the 10th day of the session you registered for, which may not be the 10th day of the term if you register for session 2 or 3. Pay close attention to the start date of your course and session to determine when you will become an enrolled student.

### About Your Bachelor's Degree

* * *

It is recommended that your bachelor's degree aligns with your chosen graduate program. If your bachelor's degree is in an unrelated field, we recommend you speak with an admissions counselor to determine your next steps.

### If Your GPA is Below 3.0

* * *

If your undergraduate GPA was less than 3.0, we ask that you provide a personal statement and a current resume along with your application. Your application package will be forwarded to the appropriate academic school Admissions Committee for further review.

## Send Your Transcripts

* * *

As part of your application, we require official copies of your undergraduate transcripts from the institution that conferred your bachelor's degree. You will also need to provide transcripts from all other schools where you earned graduate credit, if applicable. We will evaluate those credits for transfer based on equivalent TESU courses and our graduate transfer credit policy.

Doctoral programs need your bachelor's and master's degrees official transcripts.

### Graduate Academic Policies

* * *

For more information about specific graduate academic policies, including Graduate Transfer Credit policy, please visit the Graduate Catalog.


Upload Your Resume

## Meet Your Program's Requirements

* * *

In addition to the general graduate academic requirements, the following programs have additional requirements for admissions. Acceptance to TESU does not guarantee acceptance into your chosen program.

  * Master of Science in Nursing

For admission to our Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) program, you must:

    * Have a Bachelor of Science in Nursing degree from an accepted institutionally accredited institution.
    * A Bachelor of Science in Nursing degree GPA of 3.0 or higher (If your GPA was lower than a 3.0, please read the "Provide Additional Materials" section below).
    * Have an active RN license from the United States.
View MSN Program Information

  * Master of Science in Nursing - Family Nurse Practitioner

The FNP program runs on rolling admissions with six start terms each year. Applications expire after one year. Admission to NP programs is competitive, and meeting the admission criteria does not guarantee acceptance into the programs.

The FNP program is not part of the RN-BSN/MSN program. Students must apply to the FNP program and submit all required documents to be considered for admission.

Admissions Requirements

    * Active, unencumbered RN license valid in the United States
    * A conferred Bachelor of Science in Nursing degree from an accepted institutionally accredited institution
    * Current professional resume
    * Personal statement

In a 500–750-word essay, respond to the following questions. Please cite your work where applicable.

    1. Explain how you have demonstrated self-directed learning in your academic or professional experiences.
    2. Discuss your commitment to making a positive impact on your community as a Family Nurse Practitioner.
    3. Describe how you plan to utilize your professional network to build relationships with healthcare professionals in your desired practice setting and community to achieve your professional goals.

  * Master’s to Doctorate Pathway

Students enrolled in the following TESU master’s degree programs may be eligible to participate in the Master’s to Doctorate Pathway:

    * M.A. in Liberal Studies in the Learner-Designed Area of Study
    * Master of Business Administration (MBA)
    * Professional Master of Business Administration (PMBA)
    * M.S. in Management (MSM)
    * Professional M.S. in Management (PMSM)

Students may be considered for conditional admission into the Master’s to Doctorate Pathway if they:

    * Are actively enrolled in an eligible TESU master’s degree program.
    * Have completed a minimum number of 15 graduate credits toward their master’s degree.
    * Maintain a cumulative graduate GPA of 3.0 or higher.
    * Meet all admission requirements for their selected doctoral program.

Students accepted into the program will work closely with an academic advisor to develop an individualized plan of study.

#### Ed.D. Start Terms

* * *

The Ed.D. program introduces new cohorts twice each year in January and July.

View Ed.D OLCC Program Information

  * Doctor of Education (Ed.D.) in Professional Studies

For admission to our Doctor of Education (Ed.D.) in Professional Studies program, you must have:

    * 21–30 transferable doctoral credits with a cumulative GPA of 3.0.
    * Alignment with one of TESU’s approved disciplines, such as:
      * Education Administration: School, district, or higher ed leadership.
      * Human Resources and Training: Workforce development, training, employee engagement.
      * Management and Leadership: Strategic leadership, executive management.
      * Information Technology and Systems: Cybersecurity, systems management, digital transformation.
      * Emergency Management: Disaster preparedness, public safety leadership.
      * Industrial Production and Operations: Logistics, quality improvement, supply chain.
      * Social and Community Services: Nonprofit and public service leadership.

L126: We all have different reasons for wanting to return to college. This section is designed to help answer some of the questions you may have about returning to college as an adult.
L127: 
L128:   * 【67†I have earned college credits in the past. Do I have to start over?】
L129: 
L130: Not necessarily. Many colleges and universities accept transfer credits from community or county colleges, or other accredited four-year degree programs. 【46†Learn more】.
L131:   * 【68†I have a really busy life. How much time will I have to commit to earn my degree?】
L132: It depends on the programs and degree requirements of the college or university you choose. Many schools require you to attend classes on campus several evenings a week or on weekends and then prepare for projects and tests outside class hours. Some schools offer more flexible options, geared to adult learners, such as distance learning or independent self-study, which lets you work at your own pace. And yet other schools offer a combination of both on-campus and distance learning.
L133: The length of time also varies according to the number of credits, if any, you are able to transfer to your new school. The more transfer credit you have, the less coursework you will have to complete. 【29†Learn more】.
L134:   * 【69†I’ve been working in my field for 12 years. Can I get credit for what I’ve learned?】
L135: 
L136: That is a possibility. Thomas Edison State University and several other colleges allow you to take tests to demonstrate college-level knowledge or earn credits for college-level knowledge attained through employment experience, the military or other life experiences. You may even be able to earn credit for 【70†licenses and certificates】 you already may have or courses you may have taken at work. 【71†Learn more】.
L137:   * 【72†Do I have to take an entrance exam?】
L138: 
L139: Maybe. Along with a completed application, application fee, high school or college transcripts, many colleges require prospective students to submit scores from a standardized entrance examination, such as the SAT or ACT (undergraduate) or the GMAT or MAT (graduate). Schools that work primarily with adult learners may be a little more flexible in their admission requirements.
L140:   * 【73†Summer is a light time for me at work. Do I have to wait until September to begin?】
L141: 
L142: Classes at most traditional colleges begin at the start of the spring, summer or fall semester. However, if you choose a college that offers online or distance learning, or other nontraditional programs, you may be able to start classes as soon as your enrollment is complete—no matter what time of year it is. 【43†Learn more.】
L143: 
L144:   * 【74†Can I learn online while still interacting with a professor and other students?】
L145: Yes, it is possible to have both—if you choose a school that offers both traditional and nontraditional degree programs or a school that caters specifically to adult learners. Certain schools give you the option of taking courses at a distance or attending classes on campus or at an accredited college or university of your choice, and then transferring credits back to your home school. 【15†Learn more.】
L146: 
L147:   * 【75†It’s hard to predict the demands of work and family life. What if I have to take a hiatus?】
L148: You might do well at a college that recognizes your commitment to family and career, and offers flexibility for motivated adult learners. If you need to take a break from coursework for personal or professional reasons, these schools let you resume your degree program at any time, without any loss of earned credits.
L149: 
L150:   * 【76†With many financial demands, can I afford to go back to college for my degree?】
L151: Finishing your degree is an important investment in your future, and the cost depends on how many credits your school and major require, and the fee per credit hour. Tuition and fees also vary whether you decide to attend classes on campus or complete your coursework through nontraditional means such as distance learning or guided self-study. You’ll also need to allow for the costs of books and school supplies.
L152: Many colleges will help you determine if you qualify for 【37†financial assistance】 and some will even guide you through the application process for grants, 【38†scholarships】, student loans, and state and federal financial aid programs. You also may wish to ask your employer if you qualify for tuition reimbursement. 【35†Learn more】.
L153:   * 【77†Will completing my degree really help increase my earnings or get a promotion?】
L154: According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, earnings are higher and the unemployment rate is lower for people who have high levels of education. The reverse is true for the less educated American worker.
L155: The national average for annual personal income of workers 25 and older with a bachelor’s degree is approximately $23,000 higher than Americans who only have a high school education.* Earning a college degree does not automatically mean you will command a higher salary or get a promotion; however, in both the private and public sectors, education does play a factor in certain bonuses and promotions. In some cases, a degree is required to ascend to the next level.
L156: *Source: Institute for Higher Education Policy Report: the Investment Payoff/U.S. Census Bureau, Current Population Survey (CPS) March 2004 Supplement
L157: 
L158:   * 【78†How can I ensure a college or university is reputable and respected?】
L159: The academic quality of any institution is directly tied to its 【25†accreditation】, which is an independent review of a school’s educational programs to determine the education provided is of uniform and sound quality. An institution that has earned accreditation ensures that that it has met established standards of quality determined by the organization granting the accreditation.
L160: Accreditation determines a school’s eligibility for participation in federal and state financial aid programs, is important for the acceptance and transfer of college credit and is a prerequisite for many graduate programs. The most recognized and accepted type of accreditation in the United States is regional accreditation. 【79†Learn more†www.ed.gov】.
